claims.statement: The Commission reports an EU annual building-renovation rate of about 1% and says the revised EPBD requires minimum-performance trajectories plus renovation one-stop shops; as of July 2026 all 27 Member States had been sent formal notices for incomplete transposition.
The Commission defines one-stop shops as providing technical, administrative, legal, and financial help across the renovation journey, confirming that fragmented coordination is a recognized barrier.
A private control tower may win where owners need procurement execution rather than free information, but this distinction and the willingness to pay are unproven in Poland.

contrary_evidence: Publicly supported one-stop shops can provide free or subsidized advice and compete with the planning layer.
Incomplete national transposition creates uncertainty about exact Polish timing and requirements.
Housing-association voting, grants, and construction oversight can create long sales cycles and high-touch delivery.

economics.acquisition_route: At EPC handoff, independent energy assessors can send a co-branded paid next-step plan rather than a static certificate; one integration with a property manager can activate the same workflow across dozens of buildings at reserve-budget season. Revenue sharing is tied to a completed roadmap, not to favoring a construction bid.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Repeatable scopes for common building archetypes, normalized local price benchmarks, contractor quality gates, financing checklists, and verified savings reduce decision time and change orders. Portfolio purchasing and completion discipline matter more than the software dashboard itself.
fingerprint.customer: Polish housing associations and property managers responsible for portfolios of older 10-100 unit apartment buildings that lack an internal energy-renovation team.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: At EPC handoff, independent energy assessors can send a co-branded paid next-step plan rather than a static certificate; one integration with a property manager can activate the same workflow across dozens of buildings at reserve-budget season. Revenue sharing is tied to a completed roadmap, not to favoring a construction bid.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A digital survey and utility-data model produce a phased renovation plan, financing and grant checklist, tender-ready scopes, normalized bid comparison, milestone evidence, and post-project energy verification. It is an owner's control layer, not a general contractor, and starts with one repeatable building archetype.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The association pays for an independent phased roadmap and tender specification; it pays a second fixed coordination fee when members approve procurement, followed by optional annual measurement and defect-tracking fees.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An EPC, boiler failure, roof or facade project, subsidy window, high communal energy bill, or lender request forces collective owners to compare insulation, controls, heating, PV, and financing across multiple contractors.

founder_fit: Strong analytical and automation fit, with practical access to renewable installers and Polish building economics.
Can validate as a productized owner-representation service before committing capital or hiring construction crews.
Association governance and site coordination are meeting-heavy, so the model needs property-manager distribution and standardized decisions to remain founder-compatible.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Renovation Control Tower for Small Apartment Portfolios
uncertainties: Which Polish building archetype has the shortest decision cycle and highest repeatable savings.
Price that an association will pay before a grant or construction contract is secured.
Professional-liability boundary among the control tower, energy assessor, designer, and contractor.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Choose one city and one building archetype, interview ten property managers representing at least 50 buildings, and sell three paid diagnostic roadmaps to associations before offering construction coordination. Advance only if one association approves a tender and the roadmap can be produced in under two founder workdays excluding licensed design.
